text.p: Shares in Britain's Imperial Tobacco Group Plc and Gallaher Group Plc rose on Monday, reversing some of the falls seen in recent weeks.
Despite a sharp drop in the value of other equities, shares in Imperial were up 6-1/2 pence at 379-1/2 in late afternoon trading, making it the joint biggest gainer in the FT-SE 100.
Shares in Gallagher also bucked the generally soggy trend to rise 2-1/2 pence to 251.

One analyst said the stocks seemed to be recovering slightly from recent sharp setbacks in the sector, which have included worries over U.S. litigation, the impact of a strong pound on exports and the imposition of tax hikes on cigarettes in the British government's most recent budget.
He said lower prices resulting from the stronger pound's impact on the import of key ingredients was one factor supporting the stocks.
Imperial was demerged from Hanson Plc last October.
